name: vice
why: A full Commodore 64 and friends emulator, a window into old-school hardware you can run, probe, and dig into.

brief.what_it_is: VICE is a multi-machine emulator for Commodore 8-bit computers. The project says it emulates the C64, the C64DTV, the C128, the VIC20, practically all PET models, the PLUS4 and the CBM-II (aka C610/C510), and provides an extra emulator for a C64 expanded with the CMD SuperCPU. It runs on Unix, MS-DOS, Win32, OS/2, BeOS, QNX, Amiga, Syllable and Mac OS X machines, and the current release is 3.10. The brew executables are separate programs for each machine (x64sc, x128, xpet and so on), plus helpers: c1541 for disk images, cartconv for cartridges, petcat for BASIC tokenising, and vsid for playing SID music files. Input is Commodore program, disk, tape or cartridge files, and output is the emulated machine's screen and sound.
brief.why_it_exists: The project describes itself as a general-purpose emulator collection for the old 8-bit Commodore machines, and its site asks for volunteers to keep development going. The README does not state a longer motivation.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not describe the internals. It mentions a binary monitor interface, described as stable, which other projects use to build debuggers and IDE integrations. A user review says the emulation is cycle-exact and the SID sound emulation is strong, but that is the reviewer's claim, not the project's.
brief.install_notes: Homebrew installs the executables listed in the brew metadata. The project's own download page lists source tarball vice-3.10.tar.gz, Windows 64-bit builds in GTK3 and SDL2 flavours, and macOS builds for Apple Silicon and Intel (macOS 12.0+), each in GTK3 and SDL2 versions. The site recommends GTK3 over SDL2. Other platforms have separate download pages. No runtime, account or hardware is needed beyond the emulator itself. The page does not describe first-run setup, ROM requirements or configuration. Reviewers say the Windows package puts the executables deep in a shared BIN folder.
brief.standout: One package covers many Commodore machines, including a PET family that few emulators touch, and the project has its own debugger-facing binary monitor interface that outside tools build on. The SourceForge page lists it as having been Dutch Commodore user group's innovation prize winner in 2008, according to the project site.
brief.status: Maintained. The SourceForge page says last update 1 day ago and about 3,780 downloads this week. The project site has a news item dated 24 December 2025 announcing version 3.10, and SourceForge reviews are dated as recently as 2025-12-25. Development is volunteer-run and described as spare-time work.
brief.caveats: The SourceForge page is mostly site chrome and ads, so its content was thin. The executable names are cryptic (x64sc, xscpu64, x64dtv), and several user reviews complain the Windows layout and executable choices are confusing for non-programmers. Some reviews say old config and sound settings were broken in earlier releases and that the file-loading dialogs are awkward. The project is GPLv2 (the site text says 'or at your option any later version'). The brew description is 'Versatile Commodore Emulator' with no other caveats recorded.
quotes: We recommend the GTK3 user interface over SDL2.
We always need more help to keep all things going, so here is the usual call for volunteers... ;-)

judge.reason: VICE is a deep, still-maintained window into several distinct Commodore machines, with disk and cartridge tools plus a debugger-facing monitor for exploring how they work.

entry.title: VICE
entry.tldr: A family of emulators for Commodore's 8-bit computers, from the C64 to the PET, with tools for disk images, cartridges and SID music.
entry.deeper_look:
VICE is a collection of emulators for Commodore's 8-bit machines. The project lists the C64, C64DTV, C128, VIC20, practically all PET models, the PLUS4 and the CBM-II, plus a separate emulator for a C64 with the CMD SuperCPU. Each machine gets its own program: `x64sc` for the C64, `x128`, `xvic`, `xpet`, `xplus4` and so on. You feed it Commodore program, disk, tape or cartridge files, and it gives you the machine's screen and sound.

The helper tools are the part that opens things up. `c1541` works with disk images, `cartconv` converts cartridge files, `petcat` turns BASIC text into tokenised programs and back, and `vsid` plays SID music files without the rest of the machine. Together they let you look inside the file formats these computers used, not just run them.

The project also offers a binary monitor interface, which it describes as stable and which other projects use to build debuggers and IDE integrations. That makes VICE a practical target for writing and debugging code for hardware that is decades old. One user review calls the emulation cycle-exact with strong SID sound, but that is the reviewer's claim, not the project's.

Development is volunteer-run in spare time, and the site says: "We always need more help to keep all things going, so here is the usual call for volunteers... ;-)"
entry.install:
brew install vice
# GUI application (GTK3); no account or hardware needed. The brief does not cover ROM or first-run setup.
